topic: CLAUDE.md project memory in Claude Code
facts: In Claude Code, the /init command scans your project and writes a CLAUDE.md file.
Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md at the start of every session in that folder.
Put your build commands, code style and project rules in CLAUDE.md so you stop repeating them.
Press Shift+Tab in Claude Code to cycle modes until you reach plan mode.
In plan mode Claude researches and proposes a plan before it edits any files.
You approve the plan, then Claude starts making changes.
Long Claude Code sessions fill up the context window.
/compact summarizes the conversation so far and keeps working with the summary.
/clear wipes the conversation and starts fresh in the same folder.

topic: Custom slash commands in Claude Code
facts: Save a markdown file in .claude/commands/ inside your project.
The file name becomes a slash command, so review.md becomes /review.
The file holds the prompt Claude runs when you type the command.
On claude.ai, a Project groups chats with shared files and instructions.
Upload documents to the Project knowledge so every chat in it can use them.
Add project instructions once instead of pasting context into every chat.
Claude.ai lets you pick a style for how Claude writes, such as concise or explanatory.
You can create a custom style by giving Claude a sample of your own writing.
The style applies to the replies in your chats until you switch it.
Ask Claude to build something like a calculator, a quiz or a small web page.
Claude shows it as an artifact in a panel next to the chat, where you can use it.
Ask for changes in plain words and Claude updates the artifact.

topic: Connect tools to Claude Code with MCP
facts: MCP stands for Model Context Protocol, an open standard for connecting tools to AI apps.
In Claude Code you add a server with the command claude mcp add.
Once added, Claude can call that server's tools during a task.
Hooks run your own shell command at set moments, like before or after Claude uses a tool.
They are configured in Claude Code's settings.json file.
A common use is running a code formatter automatically after every file edit.
A subagent is a helper with its own instructions and its own context window.
You define one as a markdown file in .claude/agents/.
Claude can hand a focused job, like reviewing code, to that subagent.

topic: Run Claude Code from scripts with claude -p
facts: claude -p followed by a prompt runs one task and prints the answer, with no chat window.
That makes Claude Code usable inside scripts and scheduled jobs.
You can pipe a file into it, for example cat log.txt piped into claude -p with a question.
claude --continue reopens your most recent conversation in that folder.
claude --resume shows a list of past sessions to pick from.
Your earlier context comes back, so you do not have to explain the task again.

topic: Stop permission prompts in Claude Code
facts: Claude Code asks before running commands or editing files.
The /permissions command lets you allow specific tools or commands you trust.
Allowed rules are saved in settings, so the same prompt stops coming back.
Press Escape once to stop Claude in the middle of what it is doing.
Press Escape twice to go back to an earlier message and edit it.
This lets you correct the direction early instead of waiting for a wrong result.

topic: Add files to context with @ in Claude Code
facts: Type @ followed by a file path in Claude Code to point Claude at that file.
Claude reads the file before it answers.
Pointing at the exact file saves time compared with letting Claude search for it.

topic: Claude web search for cited answers
facts: Claude can search the web when web search is turned on.
Answers that use search include citations to the pages Claude read.
Ask it to cite sources so you can check each claim.
Claude.ai has connectors for apps such as Google Drive, Gmail and Google Calendar.
Once connected, Claude can find and read your documents when you ask.
You can ask questions like summarize the latest proposal in my Drive.
Extended thinking lets Claude reason step by step before it answers.
It helps on hard tasks like math, planning or tricky code.
Turn it on for hard problems and leave it off for quick questions.

topic: Use XML tags in Claude prompts
facts: Anthropic's prompting guide recommends XML tags to separate parts of a prompt.
For example, put the document inside document tags and the task outside them.
Clear separation stops Claude from mixing up your instructions and your data.
Showing Claude two or three examples of the output you want is called multishot prompting.
Examples teach format and tone better than a long description.
Make the examples varied so Claude does not copy one too closely.
Tell Claude it may say I don't know when the answer is not in the document.
Ask it to quote the exact passage before it answers.
Quotes make every answer checkable against your own file.
Claude Code has an extension for VS Code.
It runs Claude Code inside the editor, next to your files.
You can see Claude's proposed edits as diffs before you accept them.
Claude Code can run git commands for you in your project.
Ask it to look at your changes and write a clear commit message.
Review the message and the diff before you push.
A Claude skill is a folder with a SKILL.md file.
The folder can also hold scripts or templates the skill uses.
The steps in SKILL.md tell Claude when to run each script.
In ChatGPT settings, Personalization has custom instructions.
Tell ChatGPT what it should know about you and how it should respond.
The instructions apply to every new chat.
Say remember that, followed by a fact, and ChatGPT can save it to memory.
Saved memories are used in later chats.
You can view and delete memories in settings under Personalization.
A ChatGPT Project keeps related chats and files together.
You can add project instructions that apply to every chat in the project.
Files uploaded to the project are available in all of its chats.
A custom GPT is a version of ChatGPT with your own instructions and files.
You build it in the GPT builder by describing what it should do.
You can upload knowledge files and share the GPT with a link.
Canvas opens your writing or code in a separate editor next to the chat.
You can highlight one part and ask ChatGPT to change only that part.
It is useful for editing long drafts without regenerating everything.
You can ask ChatGPT to open your draft in canvas.
Deep research runs a multi-step search on the web and writes a report.
The report includes citations to its sources.
It takes longer than a normal answer, so use it for real research questions.
Choose deep research from the tools in the ChatGPT message box, then type your question.
A temporary chat does not appear in your chat history.
It does not use or create memories.
Use it for one-off questions you do not want saved.

topic: Edit images by asking in ChatGPT
facts: ChatGPT can create images from a text description.
After an image appears, ask for a specific change in plain words.
Be specific about what to keep and what to change.
ChatGPT tasks let you schedule a prompt to run later or on repeat.
For example, ask for a news summary every morning at 8.
ChatGPT sends you the result when the task runs.
Codex CLI is OpenAI's coding agent that runs in your terminal.
Install it with npm install -g @openai/codex.
Run codex inside a project folder and describe the change you want.
Codex reads instructions from a file called AGENTS.md in your repository.
Put build commands, test commands and code style rules in it.
Codex follows those rules on every task in that repo.
Codex CLI has approval modes that control what it can do without asking.
A cautious mode asks before running commands or editing files.
Use the stricter mode on code you care about, and loosen it only for throwaway work.
codex exec followed by a task runs Codex without the interactive screen.
It is meant for scripts and automation.
It prints its progress and finishes when the task is done.
Codex in ChatGPT can work on tasks in the cloud on your GitHub repositories.
You connect GitHub, pick a repo and describe the task.
Codex works in its own environment and can open a pull request for you to review.
Codex has an extension for VS Code and similar editors.
It lets you chat with Codex next to your code.
It can read the open files and propose edits.
Start a prompt by telling ChatGPT who it should act as.
Then state the goal and who the answer is for.
End with the format you want, like a table or five bullet points.
Add: ask me any questions you need before you start.
ChatGPT will ask about missing details instead of guessing.
Your answers make the final result fit what you actually need.
Upload a CSV or Excel file to ChatGPT.
Ask questions about it in plain words, like which month had the most sales.
ChatGPT can make charts from the data.
ChatGPT can search the web for recent information.
Answers from search include links to the sources.
Click the sources to check the facts before you use them.
ChatGPT agent can do multi-step tasks using its own virtual browser.
Examples are researching options and filling in a plan.
It asks for your confirmation before important actions.
ChatGPT can create a share link for a conversation.
Anyone with the link can view the chat.
Later messages you send are not added to the shared copy.
DeepSearch makes Grok search the web and X before answering.
It returns a researched answer with its sources.
Use it for questions where a quick answer is not enough.
In the Grok app, select DeepSearch in the message box before you send your question.
Think mode makes Grok reason through a problem before answering.
It is better for math, logic and planning questions.
It takes longer than a normal reply.
In the Grok app, select Think in the message box before you send your question.

topic: Ask Grok about a post on X
facts: On X you can ask Grok to explain a post.
You can also mention @grok in a reply with your question.
Grok answers using the post and its context.
Grok Imagine creates images and short videos from a text prompt.
Describe the subject, the setting and the style.
Generate a few versions and keep the best one.
Grok has a voice mode in its mobile app.
You talk and Grok answers out loud.
It is useful for hands-free questions or practicing a conversation.
Grok's settings let you add custom instructions.
Tell it how long its answers should be and what tone to use.
The instructions apply to your future chats.
Grok has a private chat option.
Private chats are not saved to your chat history.
Use it for one-off questions you do not want kept.

topic: Use the Grok API with the OpenAI SDK
facts: xAI's API is compatible with the OpenAI SDK.
Set the base URL to https://api.x.ai/v1 and use your xAI API key.
Existing OpenAI code can then call Grok models with small changes.
Developers get xAI API keys from the xAI console at console.x.ai.
Create a key and store it as an environment variable, not in your code.
Then send requests to the API at api.x.ai.

topic: Summarize a long X thread with Grok
facts: Paste a long thread or link into Grok, or ask Grok about it on X.
Ask for the main points in three bullets.
Then ask follow-up questions about the part you care about.
You can upload a file such as a PDF to Grok.
Ask questions about it in plain words.
Ask Grok to point to the part of the file each answer comes from.
Ask Grok to include links to its sources.
Open the links and check that they say what Grok claims.
This catches mistakes before you repeat them.

topic: Rewrite a post in your voice with Grok
facts: Paste two or three of your own past posts into Grok as examples.
Ask it to rewrite a new draft in the same voice.
Examples work better than describing your style.
Paste the claim and ask Grok to check it with DeepSearch.
Ask it to list sources that support and contradict the claim.
Read the sources yourself before deciding.
You can upload an image to Grok and ask for an edit.
Describe exactly what to change and what to keep.
Ask for another version if the first is not right.
